name: Old Serra'kis
summary: Old Serra'kis is an ancient, massive threshadon dwelling in the submerged subterranean waters of Blackfathom Deeps. Hidden in a flooded cave beneath the ruins, the enormous beast is lethal to any who seek it out.

sections.title: Unconquered in the Depths
sections.body: The Twilight's Hammer has made its home in the sunken Moonshrine Ruins, but the dark waters beneath the Moonshrine Sanctum hide older, wilder things. Old Serra'kis, the largest threshadon in the sunken temple, lurks in the Forgotten Pool, a flooded cave beneath the ruins where few would think to look.

sections.title: A Hidden Threat
sections.body: Reaching Old Serra'kis requires plunging deep beneath the temple floor into a flooded cavern beneath the ruins. Lacking air pockets, the cave itself is as deadly as the beast within. Those who corner him find that Serra'kis possesses an unnatural shadow-leeching resilience, draining the life from his attackers while sustaining his own vitality in the murky darkness.

faq.q: What kind of creature is Old Serra'kis?
faq.answer: Old Serra'kis is a massive, ancient threshadon—a long-necked, aquatic reptile native to the lakes and coastal waters of Azeroth.

faq.q: Why didn't the Twilight's Hammer kill him?
faq.answer: Nothing records the cult ever hunting him. Old Serra'kis lurks out of sight in the Forgotten Pool, a flooded, airless cave beneath the ruins, and is deadly to anyone who dives in after him.
He lurks in a submerged cavern beneath the water surrounding the Moonshrine Sanctum within Blackfathom Deeps. Swimmers must dive under the ruins into an airless pool to encounter him.
Beyond fighting entirely underwater without natural pockets of air, Old Serra'kis leeches shadow energy from all nearby foes to heal his own wounds throughout combat.

faq.q: Does Serra'kis serve the Twilight's Hammer?
faq.answer: No. Unlike other beasts corrupted or trained by the cult, Old Serra'kis remains a completely untamed wild predator defending his subterranean lair.

faq.q: Can you breathe during the battle with Serra'kis?
faq.answer: His enclosed cave offers no ceiling air pockets, forcing underwater fighters to either manage their breath, use magical water-breathing aid, or kite the beast out toward open water.

angles.text: Druids of the wild will find Aquatic Form indispensable when diving into the lightless pool to confront this prehistoric predator.
A warlock's ability to bestow Unending Breath turns an otherwise deadly, airless subterranean ambush into a manageable fight.
Water Breathing spells granted by spiritual communion with the elements ensure your companions don't drown while grappling with the ancient thresher.
